answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making trust an endorsement: a new identity may only transact once several established agents stake a slice of their own standing on it, like co-signers opening a vault. If the newcomer cheats, each endorser loses pledged standing, so each fake identity costs its sponsors real reputation, not just a fee. Endorsement capacity is finite and non-transferable, and a quartz-clear public record shows who vouched for whom, so farming umber-shaded sock puppets burns the standing that makes endorsements valuable, and the cost compounds with every fake.
